Whole-brain group-level contrast (emotional>neutral) during an empathic accuracy task involving watching/rating others' emotions; measures social/emotion processing.

Task involves empathic accuracy/emotion tracking rather than affiliation/attachment, bonding, or relationship-based contrasts (e.g., loved one vs stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Although stimuli are social (videos of people speaking), the contrast targets emotional vs neutral content and empathic processing rather than a social communication construct (e.g., faces vs non-faces; gaze; prosody vs non-social). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-referential judgment or self vs other contrast; participants rate the target's emotional intensity. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Contrast indexes perception/understanding of others' emotional states (empathy/mentalising) while watching targets describe emotional events vs neutral; whole-brain group-level effect in healthy adults.

Whole-brain group-level contrast (neutral>emotional) within the same social task context; reflects differential processing during social videos with reduced emotional content (e.g., DMN engagement) and still part of social-processing task manipulation.
Neutral>emotional contrast does not operationalize affiliation/attachment or bonding. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Does not specifically measure social communication; manipulation is emotionality (neutral bedroom description vs emotional story) rather than communication signals per se. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-focused processing manipulation/contrast; primarily content difference in others' videos. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Even neutral clips involve attending to/understanding another person (target) and this whole-brain contrast captures changes in processing of others when emotional mental-state content is absent vs present; still within an empathy/other-perception paradigm.
Whole-brain group-level parametric modulation by intra-individual empathic accuracy (Z-EA) during emotional clips; directly indexes social-cognitive/empathic processing variability.
Z-EA modulation reflects empathic accuracy/mentalising, not affiliation/attachment processes. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Parametric modulator is empathic accuracy rather than communication perception/production. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
EA assesses accuracy about others' emotions; no self-knowledge/agency contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Empathic accuracy is a canonical measure of understanding others' emotional/mental states; whole-brain group-level modulation by Z-EA in healthy adults.
Whole-brain group-level negative modulation by Z-EA during emotional clips; still reflects social processing mechanisms varying with empathic accuracy.
Negative EA modulation does not measure affiliation/attachment. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Negative EA modulation is not a social communication construct. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No explicit self-perception/agency/self-knowledge contrast; modulation is by EA about others. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Z-EA (empathic accuracy) indexes understanding others' emotions; negative modulation still pertains to perception/understanding of others at whole-brain group level.
Whole-brain group-level correlation between BOLD and participants' continuous ratings of the target's emotional intensity during social videos; measures dynamic social/emotion processing.
Emotional intensity tracking of a target is not affiliation/attachment/bonding. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Negative correlation with emotional intensity ratings is not a social communication-specific contrast. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Not self-referential/agency; regressor is about others. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Whole-brain group-level F-test during naturalistic viewing of social interactions; evaluates neural responses across interaction types, thus measuring social processing broadly.

Although global criteria appear met, this across-interaction-types F-test is not specifically designed to measure affiliation/attachment (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).

Interaction types include verbal vs non-verbal communicative content; an omnibus F-test across interaction categories in a social interaction viewing task indexes social communication-related processing.
Task/contrast concerns interpreting others' interactions, not self-referential judgment or self-knowledge (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Interpreting social interactions primarily involves perceiving/understanding others’ actions and mental states; an omnibus F-test across interaction types captures this construct.
Whole-brain group-level F-test across non-verbal interaction types during social interaction viewing; measures broad social processing.
Non-verbal interaction-type differences are not specifically about attachment/affiliation or bonding manipulations (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Non-verbal interaction types are a form of social communication; an omnibus test across them measures social communication processing.
No self-referential component; focuses on observing others’ interactions (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Understanding non-verbal interactions involves action/mental-state understanding of others; omnibus differences across non-verbal interaction types fit perception/understanding of others.
Whole-brain verbal > non-verbal interaction contrast during social interaction viewing; measures social processing.
Verbal vs non-verbal communication contrast does not operationalize affiliation/attachment bonding (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Directly contrasts verbal (communicative) vs non-verbal interaction types; this is a core social communication manipulation.
Contrast is about modality of others’ interactions, not self-processing (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Observing verbal interactions entails understanding others’ actions/intentions; verbal > non-verbal engages perception/understanding of others within social interaction context.
Whole-brain non-verbal > verbal interaction contrast during social interaction viewing; measures social processing broadly.
Non-verbal vs verbal interaction contrast does not specifically assess affiliation/attachment or bonding (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Contrasts non-verbal communicative interaction cues against verbal interaction cues; fits social communication processing.
No self-referential appraisal; focuses on observing others (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Non-verbal interactions require interpreting others' actions and social signals; non-verbal > verbal fits perception/understanding of others in social context.
Whole-brain contrast between non-verbal interaction subtypes (unresolved > habitual) in social interaction viewing; measures social processing.
Unresolved vs habitual interaction framing does not explicitly target affiliation/attachment/bonding constructs (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Non-verbal interaction subtype contrast concerns interpretation of non-verbal communicative dynamics; fits social communication.
Contrast concerns others' interaction dynamics, not self-knowledge/agency (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Differentiating unresolved from habitual interactions involves understanding others’ actions/mental states and social intentions; fits perception/understanding of others.
Whole-brain contrast between non-verbal interaction subtypes (habitual > unresolved) during social interaction viewing; measures social processing broadly.
Habitual vs unresolved is not a specific affiliation/attachment manipulation (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Non-verbal interaction subtype contrast pertains to processing different non-verbal communicative scenarios; fits social communication.
No self-referential processing required (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Judging habitual vs unresolved interactions involves interpreting others’ behavior and likely intentions; fits perception/understanding of others.
Whole-brain contrast (non-habitual > habitual) between non-verbal interaction types during social viewing; measures social processing.
Non-habitual vs habitual interaction contrast does not specifically operationalize bonding/attachment (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Contrasts types of non-verbal interactions/communication; fits social communication processing.
Observation of others’ interactions without self-focus (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Interpreting non-habitual interactions requires understanding others’ actions/mental states; fits perception/understanding of others.
Whole-brain contrast (non-habitual > unresolved) between non-verbal interaction types; measures social processing in a social interaction viewing task.
Contrast does not target affiliation/attachment constructs (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Differentiates non-verbal interaction scenarios; this engages processing of social communicative cues.
No self-referential judgment; focus is on others’ interactions (missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Contrast requires understanding others’ actions and implied intentions/mental states in non-verbal interactions; fits perception/understanding of others.

Fails local inclusion (PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2): no self-referential appraisal; judgments are about stimulus valence, not self traits/states.
Emotion perception from others’ facial/vocal expressions requires representing others’ affective states; main effect of emotion captures neural processing of others’ emotional cues.

Group-level whole-brain univariate contrast of partnered (interactive) vs non-partnered movement in healthy adults; task inherently involves social interaction/joint action and processing partner-related social cues (haptic joint action), engaging social cognition network (e.g., mPFC/TPJ/pSTS).

Although partnered interaction may be cooperative, the contrast is not designed to measure affiliation/attachment or social bonding (no manipulation of relationship closeness/attachment, cooperation vs competition, loved one vs stranger). Missing local criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Partnered joint action with haptic contact requires exchanging movement information/signals between partner and participant (non-verbal, non-facial communication). Contrast isolates partnering/interaction vs solo, capturing social communicative signaling/perception via touch/movement cues.
Contrast is not explicitly about self-referential judgments or agency (self vs other); it primarily manipulates presence of partner/contact. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Partnered condition requires tracking/representing the partner’s actions and likely mentalizing (pSTS/TPJ/mPFC reported); contrast targets processing of another agent during interaction vs alone.

Role-specific Leading contrast primarily reflects motor planning/self-initiated action after removing shared partnering effects; it does not directly measure social processing. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No affiliation/attachment manipulation or measure in Leading specificity contrast. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Although leading could involve signaling, the reported leading-specific map is motoric and authors find no specific signaling interaction effects; contrast not clearly measuring communication per se. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Leading specificity emphasizes self-initiation/agency and internally-driven action selection (leader generates movement), aligning with self-related agency processes.
Leading-specific contrast does not focus on perceiving/understanding the partner; it isolates self-driven motor generation. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Following specificity is externally-oriented and includes social-cognitive/perceptual components (pSTS/mPFC/TPJ reported) during joint interaction; measures social processing related to responding to partner cues.
No explicit bonding/attachment/cooperation manipulation; contrast is about sensory-guided following. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Following relies on reception/decoding of non-facial communicative cues from partner via haptic motion signals (responsive coordination).
Contrast is not self-referential/agency-focused; it is about externally guided responding to partner. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Following requires tracking and mapping the partner’s actions/intentions (action perception; understanding another agent during interaction), with reported pSTS/MT+/aIPL involvement.
Mutual condition specificity engages mentalizing and social reward networks (mPFC/TPJ/PCC/amygdala/NAc) during symmetric interaction; clearly social processing.

Despite involving cooperation-like mutuality/reward, task does not operationalize affiliation/attachment constructs (no relationship/attachment/cooperation vs competition manipulation). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Symmetric mutual coordination with partner requires ongoing bidirectional nonverbal communication/coordination cues through haptic interaction; contrast targets this mutual interactive state vs other partnered roles.
Not explicitly self-judgment/agency contrast; focuses on mutual/mentalizing processes. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Enhanced mentalizing network recruitment indicates reasoning about partner intentions/mental states during mutual interaction.

Improvisation contrast (Leading+Solo > Mutual+Alone) targets motor improvisation/sequence generation and working memory, not social processing; includes solo condition and is not specifically social. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No affiliation/attachment manipulation; improvisation vs prelearned motor sequences. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Not a communication contrast; includes solo improvisation and focuses on generation/variability. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Not explicitly self-referential/agency; it is improvisation vs fixed patterns. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Does not assess perception/understanding of others; includes solo condition and no other-related manipulation. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Self-initiation contrast ([Leading+Solo+Mutual+Alone] > Following) indexes internally generated vs externally triggered movement; not inherently social. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No affiliation/attachment component. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Not designed to measure communication; contrasts internal vs external triggering of action. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast explicitly targets self-initiated (internally driven) action vs externally driven following, aligning with agency/self-initiation processes.
Not focused on representing others; primarily self-initiation. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Joint improvisation analysis described as interaction-related contrasts/conjunctions (e.g., Leading>Solo, [Leading>Mutual]>[Solo>Alone], conjunctions) are effectively interactions/difference-of-differences; these violate global criterion against interactions/between-condition interactions for generalizability. Apply GLOBAL_E3.
Excluded due to interaction-style contrast (GLOBAL_E3) and not an affiliation/attachment task.
Excluded due to interaction-style contrast (GLOBAL_E3) even though it relates to partner signaling; not eligible under global rules.
Excluded due to interaction-style contrast (GLOBAL_E3); not a simple whole-brain main effect/within-condition map for self-processing.
Excluded due to interaction-style contrast (GLOBAL_E3) even though it concerns leading with partner vs solo.

Task involves perceiving biological motion/direction and potential social involvement, but does not measure affiliation/attachment or bonding constructs (e.g., loved one, cooperation, attachment). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Contrast reflects action/animacy perception of another agent (biological motion facing away vs toward), a core 'perception and understanding of others' construct; whole-brain group-level task contrast in healthy adults.

Healthy adult sample and group-level whole-brain task contrast during viewing of social interaction videos (reactive–aggressive > neutral), which measures processing of socially relevant interactions.
Although the task is social, this contrast targets reactive aggression vs neutral rather than affiliation/attachment/bonding processes (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).

Viewing dynamic realistic social interaction scenarios (including gestures/actions directed at the participant) engages receptive non-facial social communication cues; contrast isolates social-affective interaction processing vs neutral.

First-person perspective videos instruct participants to put themselves into the scenario (self-involvement/agency-relevant appraisal) and contrast examines neural responses during this self-referential involvement vs neutral.
Contrast involves perceiving and interpreting another person's aggressive/provocative actions and intentions in a social interaction, fitting action perception/understanding others.
Healthy adult sample and group-level whole-brain task contrast during viewing of social-positive interaction videos (social-positive > neutral), measuring social processing.
Social-positive interactions (e.g., handshake/positive approach) vs neutral index positive social affiliative responding and approach-related bonding cues.
Dynamic social-positive interactions rely on receptive interpretation of social gestures/actions (non-facial communication) vs neutral baseline.
First-person perspective with instructions to empathize/immerse implicates self-related appraisal/agency during positive interaction vs neutral.
Requires perceiving others' friendly actions/intentions in realistic interactions (action perception/mental state inference) vs neutral.
Conjunction of two group-level whole-brain social task contrasts (reactive–aggressive > neutral AND social-positive > neutral) captures shared social processing network.

Conjunction reflects shared activation for both aggressive and positive social interactions vs neutral; not specific to affiliation/attachment/bonding (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Shared activation while interpreting dynamic social interaction cues (aggressive and positive) vs neutral fits receptive social communication processing.
Both conditions are experienced from first-person perspective with self-involvement; conjunction captures common self-referential/agency-related processing vs neutral.
Both conditions require perceiving others' actions and social intent; conjunction reflects common action/mental-state perception vs neutral.
Healthy adult group-level whole-brain contrast for final phase reactive–aggressive > neutral during social interaction videos; measures social processing of affective interaction content.
Contrast is reactive aggression vs neutral and does not target affiliation/attachment/bonding (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Final-phase actions/gestures within interactions constitute non-facial communicative cues; contrast isolates processing of these social cues in aggressive context vs neutral.
Final phase depicts the observer's context-appropriate response from first-person perspective, implicating self-related agency/appraisal vs neutral.
Includes perception/interpretation of others' aggressive actions in an interaction and ensuing response; fits action perception/understanding others.
Healthy adult group-level whole-brain contrast for final phase social-positive > neutral during social interaction videos; measures social processing.
Final-phase of social-positive interactions (friendly reciprocation) vs neutral captures affiliative/approach-oriented social bonding cues.
Processing of dynamic friendly social gestures/actions (non-facial communication) in final phase vs neutral.
First-person perspective and depiction of the observer's friendly response engages self-related agency/appraisal vs neutral.
Perception of others' friendly actions/intentions within interaction in final phase vs neutral; fits understanding others.
Conjunction of final-phase reactive–aggressive > neutral and social-positive > neutral captures shared group-level whole-brain activation during social interaction processing.

Conjunction reflects overlap between positive and aggressive interactions vs neutral and is not specific to affiliation/attachment processes (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Shared processing of dynamic social interaction cues in final phase (both affective conditions) vs neutral fits receptive social communication.
Both affective conditions involve first-person self-involvement and observer response; conjunction captures common self-related appraisal/agency vs neutral.
Both affective conditions require perceiving others' actions/intent; conjunction captures common understanding-others processes vs neutral.

Healthy adult group-level whole-brain direct social condition comparison (reactive–aggressive > social-positive) during social interaction perception; measures social processing differences by affective valence/threat.
Contrast emphasizes reactive aggression relative to social-positive and does not measure affiliative bonding per se (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Directly compares two types of communicative social interaction cues (threat/provocation vs friendly) and thus measures receptive social communication processing differences.
First-person involvement in provocation vs friendly interaction likely modulates self-related appraisal/agency; direct comparison isolates that modulation.
Direct comparison requires distinguishing others' aggressive vs friendly actions/intentions (action perception/mental state inference).
Healthy adult group-level whole-brain direct social condition comparison (social-positive > reactive–aggressive) during social interaction perception; measures social processing differences.
Social-positive greater than reactive–aggressive emphasizes affiliative/approach-related social interaction content over threat, aligning with affiliation/attachment processing.
Compares receptive processing of friendly vs aggressive social communicative cues (gestures/actions) in dynamic interactions.
First-person involvement in friendly vs provocative context modulates self-referential appraisal/agency; contrast captures this difference.
Requires evaluating others' friendly vs aggressive actions/intentions (understanding others) and contrasting them.
Healthy adult group-level whole-brain direct comparison (final phase reactive–aggressive > social-positive) during social interactions; measures social processing differences.
Emphasizes aggressive/threat interaction relative to social-positive, not affiliation/attachment (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).
Final-phase social actions are communicative (non-facial) and contrast examines differences in processing aggressive vs friendly interaction cues.
Final phase depicts the observer's response from first-person perspective; aggressive vs friendly context changes self-related appraisal/agency.
Distinguishes others' aggressive vs friendly behavior/intentions in the interaction during final phase (understanding others).
Healthy adult group-level whole-brain direct comparison (final phase social-positive > reactive–aggressive) during social interactions; measures social processing differences.
Final-phase social-positive > reactive–aggressive highlights affiliative/friendly interaction processing relative to threat/aggression.
Contrasts processing of friendly vs aggressive social interaction cues (gestures/actions) in final phase, fitting receptive social communication.
First-person observer response differs between friendly and aggressive contexts; contrast captures self-related appraisal/agency modulation.
Requires interpreting others' friendly vs aggressive actions/intentions during final phase; aligns with perception/understanding of others.

Whole-brain localizer contrast (self > other) in healthy adults indexes social-cognitive self/other processing, satisfying global whole-brain criteria and social processing construct coverage.

Although whole-brain in healthy adults, the self>other trait-judgment localizer is not an affiliation/attachment task/contrast (no bonding, relationship, cooperation/competition manipulation). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Although whole-brain in healthy adults, the self>other trait-judgment localizer does not measure social communication (no communicative signals such as faces/voices/gaze). Missing local inclusion criteria SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Whole-brain localizer contrast explicitly compares self vs other trait judgments, directly measuring perception/understanding of self.

Although includes an 'other' condition, the contrast is self > other and is designed to isolate self-referential processing rather than understanding others. Missing local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Whole-brain localizer contrast (other > self) in healthy adults involves social-cognitive processing about another person (President Obama), fitting broad social processing.
Other>self trait judgments about a non-close target do not measure affiliation/attachment. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Trait-judgment contrast does not involve receptive/expressive communication signals. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast is other > self, not isolating self-perception. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 (Self > Other) and does not primarily measure self-knowledge.
Whole-brain other > self contrast from trait judgments about another person measures perception/understanding of others (evaluating traits of President Obama).

Fails GLOBAL_I2 because the main-task whole-brain contrast communication > moral is not specifically a social-processing contrast; it primarily indexes semantic/content differences (remote communication vs moral statements) rather than social processing per se. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
Communication > moral does not measure affiliation/attachment processes. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Statements about remote communication behaviors are not communicative signal processing (faces/voices/gaze) and the contrast is content-based (communication vs moral), not social communication processing. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast collapses across self/other and compares content types, so it does not measure self-perception (no Self > Other). Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Contrast collapses across self/other and compares content types, not understanding others. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Moral > communication is primarily a content/semantic/moral cognition contrast and is not clearly a social-processing contrast as defined; it does not specifically measure perception/understanding of self or others, communication, or affiliation. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.

Not a social communication task/contrast. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Collapses across self/other and contrasts moral vs communication content; not self-perception. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Collapses across self/other and contrasts moral vs communication content; not other-perception. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Whole-brain self > other (collapsing across moral/communication) is a self-referential vs other-referential contrast during a social/person-processing task, meeting broad social processing criteria.
Self > other across sentences is not an affiliation/attachment measure (no bonding/relationship manipulation). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Task involves reading statements, not processing communicative signals; contrast is self vs other relevance, not social communication. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Whole-brain self > other contrast directly measures self-referential processing/self-knowledge relative to another person.
Contrast emphasizes self over other; does not isolate understanding others. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Whole-brain other > self (collapsing across moral/communication) reflects processing of information about others relative to self, fitting broad social processing.
Other > self does not measure affiliation/attachment (no close relationship/cooperation/competition contrast). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Not a social communication contrast (no faces/voices/gaze/communicative behavior). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast is other > self, not isolating self-perception. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I2 (Self > Other).
Whole-brain other > self contrast measures processing/representation of others relative to self, aligning with perception/understanding of others.

Healthy adults viewing an emergency scene with varying numbers of bystanders; group-level whole-brain parametric effect captures neural processing of a social situation (bystander context) relevant to social processing.

Although the task is social, this contrast indexes group-size modulation of action preparation when witnessing an emergency, not affiliation/attachment (no bonding, close relationships, cooperation/competition, or attachment manipulation). Missing local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Stimuli are emergency videos but the analysis is not about communicative signal processing (faces, gaze, speech, gestures) and clips were blurred to reduce facial information; contrast is group-size parametric effect. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-referential judgment, agency, or self-knowledge manipulation/contrast; parametric bystander effect during observation. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Participants perceive and interpret others in a social emergency (person fainting plus bystanders); parametric group-size effect reflects processing of others' actions/states in a social context, fitting perception/understanding of others.

Healthy adults; group-level whole-brain parametric increase with group size while viewing a social emergency scene with bystanders, constituting social-context processing (even if partly driven by visual complexity).

Contrast reflects parametric effect of number of bystanders on brain activity, not affiliative bonding/attachment or relationship-based processing. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
No explicit communicative signal processing contrast (e.g., faces/gaze/voice/gesture) and analysis targets group-size modulation; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-referential or agency manipulation; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Viewing others in an emergency with varying bystander group size engages perception of others' actions/states; parametric modulation with group size fits perception/understanding of others even if effects localize to visual-attention regions.

Control contrast compares visually altered control movies to bystander conditions to assess visual complexity rather than social processing per se. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2 (does not measure social processing).
This is a visual control (control > bystander) and does not index affiliation/attachment. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Not a communication contrast; it is a visual-control comparison. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-processing manipulation; visual control contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Although scenes contain people, this contrast is intended to quantify visual complexity (inverted/reversed control vs bystander) rather than understanding others. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 (does not measure perception/understanding of others).
Whole-brain group-level contrast of witnessing an emergency (fainting/falling) vs non-emergency standing scenario; directly probes responses to socially relevant distress/emergency cues.
Emergency observation does not manipulate affiliative bonds, attachment, or cooperative/competitive relationship context. Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Contrast is emergency vs standing and not focused on communicative cue processing; facial info was blurred. Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-referential judgments; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Contrast reflects perception of another person's state/action (fainting/falling) vs standing, fitting action perception and understanding of others in a distress context.

Standing > falling is primarily a visual/motion content comparison and does not cleanly index social processing; it is the inverse of the emergency contrast and interpreted in the paper as visual-region differences. Missing SOCIAL_PROCESSING_ALL_I2.
No affiliation/attachment manipulation; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Not a social communication contrast; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
No self-related processing; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Although a person is shown, standing > falling does not operationalize understanding others' states; it likely reflects low-level visual/motion differences and is not a targeted others-perception contrast. Missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.

Healthy adult sample and group-level whole-brain task contrast (Imitating > rest) during an online reciprocal imitation social interaction; measures social interaction/action understanding.

Task involves imitation/interaction but does not measure affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., bonding, close relationships, cooperation/competition outcomes). Missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Imitating hand gestures in real-time with a partner is non-facial social communication (production and reception of gestural signals) in a group-level whole-brain contrast.
Although interactive, the contrast does not specifically target self-referential processing or agency (e.g., self vs other judgments). Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Imitating requires perception/understanding of another person's actions and intentions in an interactive context; whole-brain group contrast supports inclusion for action perception/understanding others.
Healthy adult sample and group-level whole-brain task contrast (Being imitated > rest) during online social interaction; measures social processing in reciprocal imitation.

Being imitated is part of a bidirectional gestural exchange (non-facial social communication) with receptive/interactive components at whole-brain group level.
Contrast does not isolate self-agency/self-referential judgments; primarily an interaction condition vs rest. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Contrast captures neural response to receiving romantic interest vs rejection, directly relevant to affiliative/attachment-related social reward and bonding cues.

Receiving acceptance/rejection about oneself is self-relevant social evaluation and engages self-referential appraisal of one's desirability; thus measures perception/understanding of self in a social context.
Inferring/processing another person's intention toward the participant (interest vs rejection) requires understanding others' mental states and evaluative stance.
Whole-brain group-level contrast in healthy adults during social evaluative feedback; tests response to rejection (no) relative to acceptance (yes).
Rejection vs acceptance from potential romantic partners pertains to affiliative reward/punishment relevant to bonding/attachment.

Rejection (no) vs acceptance (yes) constitutes self-relevant evaluative feedback affecting self-appraisal/desirability beliefs.
Outcome indicates the partner's intention toward participant; processing rejection entails interpreting others' social stance/mental state.
Whole-brain group-level mismatch>match contrast during romantic evaluation task; measures processing of violated social expectations in interaction context.
Mismatch (rejection or unrequited interest) reflects disruption/violation of reciprocal affiliative outcomes in a romantic context, relevant to affiliative learning.
Mismatch vs match indexes expectancy violation/mentalizing rather than communication signal processing. Missing local inclusion: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1, SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Mismatch outcomes require updating self-relevant beliefs (e.g., whether others reciprocate one's interest / one's desirability) and appraising self in response to feedback.

Whole-brain group-level parametric effect (unsigned social prediction error) during partner decision phase in a social interaction task; measures social learning from evaluative feedback.

Parametric regressor indexes surprise/learning, not communication modality processing. Missing local inclusion: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1, SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Model operationalizes learning about one's own desirability (self-relevant expectation updating) from others' feedback.
Prediction errors are computed over others' decisions/intentions toward the participant, implicating understanding and updating beliefs about others' social actions.
Whole-brain group-level contrast at face/anticipation phase (partners participant said yes>no) in a social romantic context; measures anticipatory processing of socially relevant partners.
Yes>no partners reflects romantic interest/approach toward potential affiliative bonds and anticipation of reciprocal interest.

Whole-brain group-level contrast (partners given no>yes) during a social romantic task; captures processing of socially relevant partners differing in participant interest.

Whole-brain group-level contrast (mutual yes match > unrequited) during romantic feedback; measures social reward value conditional on reciprocity.
Directly measures neural response to reciprocal romantic interest (affiliative bonding signal) vs interest from undesired partner.
Outcome contrast about reciprocity/value, not communication decoding. Missing local inclusion: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1, SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Match vs unrequited differs in whether participant's own interest is reciprocated, a self-relevant social-evaluative outcome tied to self-appraisal.
Contrast hinges on integrating partner's intention (yes) with participant's own stance, supporting representation of others' preference toward self within social context.
Whole-brain group-level contrast (rejection>disinterest) during romantic feedback; measures processing of negative social feedback when it conflicts with own interest.
Rejection from a desired partner (vs mutual no) is a salient affiliative/attachment-relevant negative outcome in romantic bonding context.
Contrast is about social evaluative outcome, not communicative signal processing. Missing local inclusion: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1, SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Rejection (vs mutual disinterest) provides self-relevant negative evaluation affecting self-worth/desirability appraisal.
Requires processing the partner's negative intention toward participant in context of participant's own interest; involves understanding others' evaluative stance.

Healthy adults performed an implicit social evaluation task (gender judgment on faces with learned moral status); this whole-brain group contrast (affective/cooperator+defector vs neutral faces) indexes social processing of socially salient others.

Contrast targets faces of interaction partners who acquired cooperative/defective reputations through reciprocal exchange learning, tapping cooperation/fairness-related affiliative valuation vs neutral baseline.

Although faces are viewed, the contrast is not about communicative signals (e.g., expression/gaze) or face vs non-face; it is about learned moral status/affective social value. Thus Social Communication construct is not directly measured (fails SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2).
No self-referential judgment, agency, or self-knowledge manipulation; contrast concerns evaluation of others' moral status (fails PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Affective vs neutral faces reflects perception/understanding of others' traits (fair/unfair) learned from social interaction, i.e., evaluating others' dispositions.
Whole-brain group contrast in healthy adults comparing cooperator vs neutral faces measures processing of socially learned moral status and social reward value of others.
Cooperator vs neutral isolates responses to cooperative partners (reciprocal cooperation), a core affiliation/cooperation construct.
Stimuli are faces but the contrast is not communicative processing (no emotion/gaze/face vs non-face); it is social learning/moral status (fails SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2).
No self-focused processing; contrast concerns others' cooperativeness (fails PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Cooperator vs neutral measures representation of others' traits/dispositions (cooperative reputation) acquired through interaction.
Whole-brain group contrast in healthy adults comparing defector vs neutral faces indexes processing of socially learned unfairness/cheating—social evaluation of others.
Defector vs neutral targets violation of reciprocity/unfair social partner, within cooperation/competition domain relevant to affiliation/attachment constructs.
Not a communicative contrast (no facial expression/gaze communication or face vs non-face); rather moral status of partner (fails SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2).
No self-referential component; evaluates others' defection (fails PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).
Defector vs neutral captures perception/understanding of others' negative trait (unfair/defecting) learned from interaction.

Healthy adults; whole-brain group contrast (intentional > nonintentional cooperator faces) tests modulation of face processing by attributed intentionality/moral agency, a social-cognitive manipulation.
Contrast concerns cooperative partners with moral agency vs scripted behavior; still within cooperation-based affiliative valuation and social bonding learning context.
Faces are presented but the key manipulation is attributed intentionality, not reception/production of communicative cues (fails SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2).
No self-related judgments or agency of self; manipulation is about others' intentionality (fails PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2).

Intentional > nonintentional cooperators directly targets understanding others as intentional agents (mental-state attribution/animacy-like intentionality), fitting perception/understanding of others.

Healthy adults; group-level whole-brain voxelwise conjunction of task-evoked contrasts during anticipation and performance of interpersonal touch (human vs fake hand), which is a social interaction-related manipulation.

Task involves interpersonal touch (an affiliative social behavior) and contrast isolates animate (human) vs inanimate (fake) target during touch; captures affiliative/attachment-relevant social bonding behavior rather than generic somatosensation.

Healthy adults performed a whole-brain, group-level task contrast comparing internal vs external causal attributions for social events, which measures social causal reasoning/attribution.

Although stimuli involve friends and social events, the contrast targets causal attribution/self-responsibility rather than affiliation/attachment bonding or relationship formation; local inclusion criteria are not met (AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).

Task involves reading and imagining scenarios and making attribution judgments, not receptive/expressive social communication (e.g., faces, gaze, gestures); missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Internal (vs external) attributions index self-responsibility/agency judgments about the self as the cause of social events, fitting Perception/Understanding of Self (agency).

While external attributions can involve others, this specific contrast is Internal > External, emphasizing self-responsibility rather than representing/inferring others' states; missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Healthy adults; whole-brain group-level task contrast External > Internal during causal attribution of social events, capturing social causal reasoning about others/situations.
Contrast reflects attributing causality to others/situations, not attachment/affiliative bonding processes; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
No social-communicative signal processing (faces/gaze/gestures/prosody) is manipulated; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
External > Internal emphasizes other/situation responsibility rather than self-agency/self-knowledge; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
External attributions to another person/situation reflect judgments about others as causal agents in social events, aligning with understanding others' intentions/actions.
Whole-brain group-level contrast isolates self-serving attribution pattern (internal-positive + external-negative) during social-event causal reasoning, a social-cognitive process.
Self-serving bias concerns motivational attributional style/self-esteem regulation, not affiliative bonding or attachment constructs; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
No social communication cues are processed/produced; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Self-serving bias includes internal attributions for positive events (self-enhancing) and thus involves self-evaluative/self-agency-related processing about oneself as cause.
Self-serving bias also includes external attributions for negative events often assigning responsibility to others/situation, engaging representations of others as causal agents in social events.
Whole-brain group-level contrast of non-self-serving attributions (internal-negative + external-positive) during social causal reasoning; this is social processing.
Non-self-serving attribution style is not an affiliation/attachment bonding measure; missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
Task does not manipulate communicative signal reception/production; missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Non-self-serving pattern also includes external attributions for positive events (crediting others/situation), involving judgments about others/situational causes in social outcomes.
